subject.title: Bug: Built-in dreaming system contaminates agent identity in multi-agent setups

question: Should shared-workspace Dreaming be treated as a hard per-agent security boundary, or is some workspace-level pooling an intentional product mode?
rationale: Current source still pools agents by workspace, the report describes sensitive cross-agent memory contamination, and the open fix paths include public config/API and security-boundary tradeoffs that require maintainer intent before merge.

options.title: Require Per-Agent Isolation
options.body: Treat every shared-workspace Dreaming run as agent-scoped by default and require explicit, documented opt-in for any shared corpus behavior.

options.title: Accept Workspace-Level Pooling
options.body: Document shared-workspace Dreaming as expected behavior and move isolation to per-agent workspace/config guidance.

recommendation.title: Require Per-Agent Isolation
recommendation.body: Treat every shared-workspace Dreaming run as agent-scoped by default and require explicit, documented opt-in for any shared corpus behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue is assigned to vincentkoc and their comments narrowed the intended-behavior question for shared-workspace Dreaming.
